title: What is one hundredth split into ten equal parts?
description: One hundredth of a unit is split into ten equal parts, and the parts in a whole unit are counted. The new part is named, and the place values are written as a ladder from one thousand down to a thousandth, ten times at each step. Keeko's doubt is that ten is added to a hundred.
teaching_notes: One idea: a hundred hundredths, each split into ten, make a thousand parts, each one thousandth of a unit. Watch for students who add ten to a hundred instead of multiplying.

source: Split one hundredth into 10 equal parts. What is one part ca
video_script.why: The child knows tenths and hundredths and now splits once more to meet the next smaller place.
video_script.substitution: Splitting a hundredth into ten parts gives a thousandth, and a unit holds a thousand of them.
video_script.anchor: a unit bar with one hundredth magnified and split into ten equal parts
video_script.wrong_move: adds ten to a hundred instead of multiplying them
video_script.payoff_line: One part is one thousandth of a unit

final_answer.value: 1/1000 of a unit, one thousandth; 1000 of them make a unit
final_answer.spoken: one thousandth of a unit, and one thousand of them make a unit

video_script.fraction_reading: one hundredth and one thousandth are said as words
hold_back: 1/1000 of a unit, one thousandth; 1000 of them make a unit
maths_rules: each hundredth is split into 10 equal parts, so 100 x 10 = 1000 parts in a unit
each part is 1/1000 of a unit, one thousandth
one step left multiplies by 10; one step right divides by 10
the slip: 100 + 10 = 110 adds, but each of the 100 hundredths holds its own 10 parts
video_script.design: One unit bar with one hundredth magnified; the count builds in the working band, then the ladder of places appears, and Keeko's doubt strikes out the added count.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a very small part of a unit.
<bookmark mark='tiny'/>Take one hundredth of a unit and split it into ten equal parts.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many of these new parts make a whole unit?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside it as the child
a unit bar cut into 100 equal parts, each 1/100; one hundredth is magnified beside the bar

marks.bar: the unit bar is cut into 100 equal parts
marks.hundredth: one part is magnified and labelled 1/100

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Here is a unit bar cut into one hundred equal parts.
<bookmark mark='hundredth'/>Each part is one hundredth of the unit. We magnify one hundredth to see it clearly.

beats.on_screen: Given: one hundredth of a unit is split into 10 equal parts
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one hundredth of a unit is split into ten equal parts.

beats.on_screen: To find: the name of one part, how many make a unit, and the ladder of places from 1000 down
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to name one part and count how many make a unit.
We also write the ladder of place values from one thousand downwards.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: a unit has 100 hundredths, and each is split into 10 parts, so the unit has 100 x 10 parts
narration: <bookmark mark='hundreds'/>Step one, count the new parts in a unit. A unit has one hundred hundredths.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Each hundredth is split into ten parts, so we multiply one hundred by ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 1000 parts make a unit, so each part is 1/1000 of a unit, called one thousandth

marks.name: 1/1000 is written
marks.called: the part is named one thousandth

narration: <bookmark mark='name'/>Step two, name the part. One thousand such parts fill the unit, so each is one part in a thousand.
<bookmark mark='called'/>Such a part is called one thousandth of a unit.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: ladder 1000, 100, 10, 1, 1/10, 1/100, 1/1000; one step left x 10, one step right divided by 10

marks.ladder: the ladder of places is written from 1000 to 1/1000
marks.arrows: arrows show x 10 to the left and divided by 10 to the right

narration: <bookmark mark='ladder'/>Step three, write the ladder of places. It goes one thousand, one hundred, ten, one, one tenth, one hundredth, one thousandth.
<bookmark mark='arrows'/>One step to the left multiplies by ten, and one step to the right divides by ten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1/1000 of a unit, one thousandth; 1000 of them make a unit
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One part is one thousandth of a unit, and one thousand of them make a unit.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the unit bar
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 100 + 10 = 110 appears and is struck out; each of the 100 hundredths shows its own 10 parts; 100 x 10 is written

marks.fix: each hundredth shows its own 10 parts and the sum is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a unit has one hundred and ten parts, because a hundred and ten more make that.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But each of the hundred hundredths holds ten parts of its own. That is a hundred groups of ten, so we multiply.
